item.title: A frame-indifferent rank-one convex function in three dimensions which is not quasiconvex
item.description: arXiv:2610.31886v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a function $W:\mathbb{R}^{3\times3}\to\mathbb{R}$ which is frame-indifferent, $W(QF)=W(F)$ for all $Q\in\mathrm{SO}(3)$, rank-one convex, but not quasiconvex. In a neighbourhood of $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ the function is an explicit polynomial of degree four in the strain $F^TF-\mathrm{Id}$; the failure of quasiconvexity occurs at $F=\mathrm{Id}$ through a third-order mechanism of \v{S}ver\'ak type, with test functions whose gradients are arbitrarily close to $\mathrm{Id}$. The polynomial is obtained from a geometrically linear example, a rank-one convex, non-quasiconvex quartic polynomial of the symmetric part of the gradient, by evaluating it at the strain $\frac12(F^TF-\mathrm{Id})$, adding a uniaxial prestress and a cubic correction, and enlarging the quartic term. The local function is extended to all of $\mathbb{R}^{3\times3}$ by adding a frame-indifferent polyconvex function which vanishes near $\mathrm{SO}(3)$. This work was carried out with the assistance of the AI model Claude Opus 5.5; the proofs of the main results have been formally verified in Lean 4.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Conti, Georg Dolzmann, Patrick Dondl

item.title: Global regularity for 3D large spherically symmetric degenerate compressible Navier-Stokes equations with superlinear BD viscosity and far-field vacuum
item.description: arXiv:2610.32062v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Superlinear density-dependent viscosity presents a fundamental obstacle of global regularity to the compressible Navier-Stokes equations in the presence of far-field vacuum: the viscous diffusion vanishes at infinity, so excluding vacuum on bounded sets does not suffice to control the flow globally. For $\alpha\in (1,11.7)$ and $\gamma\in [2\alpha-1,3\alpha-1)$ , we establish global regularity for arbitrarily large, strong, finite-mass initial data with positive density at every finite point and vacuum at infinity. First, we introduce new rescalsed variables regarding the velocity, effective velocity and mass, then we exploit several novel quantities near the center and employ a refined maximum principle to establish the Lipschitz continuity of the velocity at the center-thereby resolving the singularity of the velocity gradient. Another key mechanism is a quantitative control of material volume distortion that remains effective in the vacuum tail. Conservative estimates for the physical and effective velocity gradients yield uniformly vanishing exterior variation tails. These estimates identify a material trajectory with small cumulative Jacobian variation and lead to two-sided bounds for the exterior volume Jacobian, making the evolving density comparable to its initial value along particle paths. On spatial scales determined by the initial density, the resulting degenerate equations admit uniform parabolic estimates that recover control of the physical deformation without a global density lower bound. Combined with compact positivity estimates and a one-sided Glaeser inequality, this closes a homogeneous continuation argument without imposing $L^2$-integrability on the density powers themselves. The solutions conserve mass, preserve far-field vacuum, and remain smooth and strictly positive on every compact spacetime cylinder.
item.dc:creator: Xiangdi Huang, Bingshu Li

item.title: Global recovery of a scalar diffusivity from a single final state
item.description: arXiv:2610.32063v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove global uniqueness and Lipschitz stability for a scalar diffusivity in the heat equation from a single final state at any prescribed positive time. On each prescribed uniformly elliptic $C^{1,\alpha}$-bounded class with known coefficient boundary values, we choose a constant initial datum and a spatially constant exponential boundary input that work for the entire class. The result holds on smooth bounded connected domains in every dimension $n\ge2$ and gives an affirmative answer to \cite[Problem~8.2]{Alessandrini} within these classes. The stability estimate controls the $L^2$ diffusivity difference by the $H^2$ final-state difference, and this data norm is optimal within the Sobolev scale for the chosen experiment.
item.dc:creator: Ching-Lung Lin, Yi-Hsuan Lin

item.title: Weighted and nonlocal Poisson equations on domains with capacity density conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.32070v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for global H\"{o}lder solvability of weighted Poisson equations and related fractional problems. On domains satisfying a capacity density condition, a nonnegative measure with bounded support depth admits a bounded globally H\"{o}lder continuous zero-boundary solution if and only if it satisfies an interior Morrey-type growth condition. Conversely, uniform boundary decay estimates for solutions with localized nonnegative sources characterize the capacity density condition. Analogous characterizations are established for the restricted and spectral fractional Laplacians. Our approach is based on weighted strong barriers and also yields two-weight Hardy inequalities, compact trace embeddings, and global H\"{o}lder solvability for nonlinear Dirichlet-to-Neumann operators.
item.dc:creator: Takanobu Hara

item.title: Well-posedness for $p(x)$-Laplacian parabolic equations under a multiple-regime setting on an annulus
item.description: arXiv:2610.32083v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes an energy-variational framework for the well-posedness of the initial boundary value problem of the parabolic equation with variable exponents on an annulus, under the multiple-regime setting consisting of the subcritical, critical and supercritical regimes of the variable exponents. The multiple-regime setting leads to the appearance of the critical and supercritical regions of positive measure, which cause the failure of the classical Sobolev embedding and the lack of compactness. To address the challenges posed by multiple regimes to well-posedness within the energy framework, we recover the compact Sobolev embedding for a class of radially symmetric functions by the Strauss inequality and obtain the local existence of the solution via the combination of the subdifferential technique and the Principle of Symmetric Criticality for any given radially symmetric initial data. Additionally, the uniqueness result is also given with the recovered Sobolev embedding. Moreover, examining the impact on well-posedness of solutions caused by the variable exponents crossing three sensitive regions, we establish a variational structure of the potential well theory for the evolution equation under the multiple-regime setting on the annulus. For subcritical and critical initial energy levels, we consider the non-positive and positive initial energy cases separately. We obtain the finite-time blow-up of the solution with non-positive initial energy and the threshold condition for global existence and finite-time blow-up of the solution with positive initial energy. For supercritical initial energy level, several sufficient criteria for the global existence and finite-time blow-up of the solution are given. Finally, the above results, including global existence and finite-time blow-up, are generalized to a more general locally symmetric domain containing an annulus.
item.dc:creator: Yitian Wang, Runzhang Xu, Chao Yang

item.title: Linear Stability and a Turning Point Principle for Barotropic Liquid Stars with a Free Boundary in General Relativity
item.description: arXiv:2610.32138v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the linear stability of spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat steady states of the Einstein-Euler system describing a liquid star surrounded by vacuum. The equation of state has positive surface density, positive causal sound speed, and an asymptotically linear high-density limit. We construct the equilibrium family and derive the linearized equation with a Robin boundary condition. The linearized operator has discrete real spectrum, and its negative Morse index equals the number of growing modes. We prove that the linearized operator around steady states with large central redshift admits a growing mode, while such growing modes do not exist for steady states with small central redshift. A parameter derivative of the equilibrium family provides a regular interior zero solution of the linearized equation, whose boundary defect is a nonzero multiple of the parameter derivative of the total mass. This gives a turning point principle: the kernel is one-dimensional precisely at mass critical points, and the sign of the crossing eigenvalue is determined by the bending of the mass-radius curve.
item.dc:creator: Zeming Hao, Jianchao Xu

item.title: Coupling perturbations of the conformal Einstein-Dirac system on round spheres
item.description: arXiv:2610.32172v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the conformal Einstein-Dirac system on the round sphere $S^m$, $m\geq3$, with coupling coefficient $1+\eps k$, where $k\in C^2(S^m,\R)$ and $\eps$ is small. Morse and degree conditions yield solutions with positive scalar component, and a generic nondegeneracy condition gives multiplicity modulo spinorial symmetries. For a suitable fixed coefficient, we obtain a noncompact solution sequence with infinitely many distinct energy values. A Kazdan-Warner identity gives nonexistence for a smooth Morse potential and its small $C^2$-perturbations, even with positive coupling. The existence proofs use a local reduction in the interior of the positive cone, accommodating the negative powers occurring when $m\geq5$.
item.dc:creator: Ke Xu, Tian Xu, Minbo Yang

item.title: Gagliardo--Nirenberg extremals on manifolds with small holes
item.description: arXiv:2610.32173v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the sharp homogeneous Dirichlet Gagliardo--Nirenberg quotient on a closed Riemannian manifold with holes of small capacity and connected complements. For each fixed exponent $2<q<2^*$, the nonnegative $L^2$-normalized extremal exists and is unique when the first Dirichlet eigenvalue $\lambda_D$ is sufficiently small. If the ambient volume is $V$ and $\beta=n(q-2)/2$, the sharp constant satisfies $C_D=V^{1-q/2}\lambda_D^{-\beta/2}(1+O(\lambda_D))$. For the normalized first eigenfunction $\varphi_D$, we obtain $\|u_D-\varphi_D\|_{H^1}=O(\lambda_D^{3/2})$ and $C_D/W_{M_D}(\varphi_D)=1+O(\lambda_D^2)$, together with a quantitative stability estimate in terms of the relative deficit. The constants depend only on the ambient manifold and the exponent. On general compact manifolds with Dirichlet boundary conditions, we prove compactness above the Euclidean sharp constant and describe concentration at equality. Positive scalar curvature at one interior point implies attainment. For the $L^2$-critical nonlinear Schr\"odinger energy, the mass threshold for negative energy tends to zero as the capacity of the holes tends to zero, whereas the threshold for unboundedness below is unchanged.
item.dc:creator: Mayukh Mukherjee, Utsab Sarkar

item.title: Well-posedness for the Cubic Nonlinear Schr\"odinger Equation With Nonlinearity Supported on a Hypersurface
item.description: arXiv:2610.32180v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the 2-d cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation with nonlinearity supported on a line or a sphere is globally well-posed in \(H^1(\mathbb{R}^2)\). For higher dimensions, we prove that the equation with hyperplane-supported nonlinearity is locally well-posed in suitable anisotropic Sobolev spaces. We also prove that the equation with sphere-supported nonlinearity is globally well-posed in \(H^1(\mathbb{R}^n)\) for radial data.
item.dc:creator: Xilin Chen, Jianlei Huang

item.title: Semilinear Schr\"{o}dinger equation with harmonic potential and combined power-type nonlinearities
item.description: arXiv:2610.32274v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Cauchy problem for the semilinear Schr\"{o}dinger equation with a harmonic potential and combined power-type nonlinearities. The goal is to classify initial data that lead to either global existence or blowup solutions by using an enhanced cross-constrained variational theory. First, we review and analyze this variational approach, pinpointing the main issue for our specific problem. We then introduce new variational structures by carefully selecting terms in the energy functional and adjusting their weights, enabling us to create eight cross-constrained variational combinations and related manifolds to distinguish initial data that result in global solutions or finite-time blowup. Using these structures, we examine three initial energy levels: negative, non-negative low, and high energy. Notably, we prove that for any initial data with negative energy, solutions blow up in finite time regardless of their size. Throughout the study, we utilize these new variational frameworks and functionals to systematically classify initial data for global existence or finite-time blowup. We highlight the comprehensiveness of our approach as we analyze numerous combinations of the energy and mass terms, despite the complexity involved. Interestingly, we find that when initial energy is minimized, classifications based on different functionals coincide. For high initial energy, an unresolved issue even for the standard Schr\"{o}dinger equation, we develop a strategy controlling bounds of energy to classify the solution dynamics, including global existence or blowup, for our model. We also provide a complete proof for the standard case addressing this open problem.
item.dc:creator: Jiangbo Han, Runzhang Xu, Chao Yang

item.title: Geometry property of stochastic parabolic equations and Pr\'{e}kopa-Leindler inequality on bounded domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.32288v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the preservation of spatial concavity and log-concavity for stochastic parabolic equations posed on bounded convex domains. For the linear noise, by using Minkowski convolutions, we establish the convexity preservation of solution almost surely. For the nonlinear noise, by using It\^{o} formula, the impact of noise is given. Moreover, we establish the relationship between the weighted (stochastic) Pr\'{e}kopa-Leindler inequality and properties of (stochastic) parabolic equation on bounded domain, which is new even for deterministic case.
item.dc:creator: Guangying Lv

item.title: Optimal time decay of the Boltzmann equation with cutoff soft potentials in the whole space
item.description: arXiv:2610.32296v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Since Strain's work \cite{Strain-2012-KRM} on almost optimal time decay rates for the microscopic part of perturbative classical solutions to the Boltzmann system with soft potentials via the time-velocity splitting method, how to obtain the optimal decay of the microscopic part has remained unsolved. In this paper, we resolve this problem by developing a nonlinear energy estimate method different from the time-velocity splitting approach. The proof relies on a combination of a hierarchy of time-weighted energy estimates, the damping factor \(e^{-\nu(v)(t-\tau)}\), and a dyadic decomposition of velocity space.
item.dc:creator: Yuanjie Lei, Xiongju Wei, Tong Yang, Huijiang Zhao

item.title: Peaking self-similar solutions and continuation after blow-up for a quasilinear Hardy-H\'enon equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.32304v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the quasilinear Hardy-H\'enon equation $$ u_t=\Delta u^m+|x|^{\sigma}u^p, \quad (x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^N\times(0,T), $$ in the range of exponents and dimension $$ N\geq3, \quad \sigma\in(-2,\infty), \quad m>1, \quad p>p_S(\sigma)=\frac{m(N+2\sigma+2)}{N-2}. $$ We establish sharp ranges of exponents $(m,p,\sigma)$ guaranteeing existence of \emph{peaking solutions} in backward self-similar form $$ u(x,t)=(T-t)^{-\alpha}f(|x|(T-t)^{-\beta}). $$ By peaking solutions we understand solutions blowing up at a finite time $T\in(0,\infty)$ but allowing for a continuation after the blow-up time. As a remarkable outcome, a number of ranges of exponents $\sigma$ and $m$ for which peaking solutions exist for any $p>p_S(\sigma)$ are deduced, contrasting to the previously considered exponent $\sigma=0$, where a Lepin-type critical exponent $p_L$ provides an upper bound for $p$.
item.dc:creator: Razvan Gabriel Iagar, Ariel S\'anchez, Erik Sarri\'on-Pedralva

item.title: Bilinear Strichartz estimates on the hyperbolic space and the cubic NLS
item.description: arXiv:2610.32358v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove bilinear Strichartz estimates for the Schr\"odinger equation on the hyperbolic space. These bilinear estimates are then applied, as part of an I-method argument, to establish global well-posedness for the cubic defocusing nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation on the hyperbolic plane for regularities above 4/7. The I-method is implemented in physical space using a heat-based modified energy.
item.dc:creator: Cristian Gavrus

item.title: Energies with values in networks and geometric quasiconvexity
item.description:

item.dc:creator: Andrea Braides, Jan Kristensen, Sergio Scalabrino

item.title: Uniform Regularity for the Compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson System under Navier-Slip Boundary Conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.32454v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish the existence of a local-in-time strong solution to the compressible Navier--Stokes--Poisson system in a three-dimensional bounded smooth domain, subject to the general Navier--slip boundary condition. The solution is shown to be uniformly bounded in conormal Sobolev spaces, with uniform regularity estimates that are independent of the viscosity coefficients. As a consequence, we obtain the inviscid limit to the corresponding compressible Euler--Poisson system via a strong compactness argument.
item.dc:creator: Hairong Liu, Jinlong Wu

item.title: Characterization of intrinsic parabolic Harnack inequalities for doubly nonlinear equations of slow diffusion type
item.description: arXiv:2610.32496v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize metric measure spaces that satisfy intrinsic parabolic Harnack inequalities for doubly nonlinear equations of slow diffusion type. The considered parabolic Harnack inequalities are intrinsic in the sense that the waiting time depends on the solution. Our main results shows that in a metric measure space with a doubling measure, such an intrinsic parabolic Harnack inequality holds if and only if a Poincar\'e inequality holds. We thus show that estimates in scale and function dependent intrinsic geometries can characterize scale and location invariant functional inequalities.
item.dc:creator: Theo Elenius

item.title: New time-periodic solutions to the cubic conformal wave equation on $\mathbb{S}^{3}$: I Spherical symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2610.32600v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a rigorous construction of novel time-periodic solutions to the radially symmetric cubic conformal wave equation on the Einstein cylinder $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{S}^{3}$. Their existence, hinted by the earlier numerical studies (arXiv:2504.10513), complements prior results on Cantor sets of infinitesimally small solutions. Our proof, based on the contraction principle, requires extensive computations that are performed on a computer by the means of rational arithmetic. We are able to significantly reduce their amount by a thorough analysis of the inverse of the associated linear operator, leading to sharper analytical bounds, as well as introduction of simplified versions of certain relevant operators. We provide examples of three solutions with specific frequency; however, our techniques and tools can be directly adapted to prove the existence of other solutions conjectured in (arXiv:2504.10513).
item.dc:creator: Filip Ficek, Maciej Maliborski

item.title: From kinetic activation dynamics to Holling type reaction-diffusion predator-prey systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.32603v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a kinetic model of predator-prey dynamics in which predation is characterized by a sequence of behavioral transitions. Prey and predators are described by distribution functions in phase space, with the predator population further structured into internal states corresponding to inactive, active, and saturated individuals. We show that different macroscopic functional responses emerge from distinct mechanisms governing predator activation. More precisely, activation driven uniquely by pairwise encounters leads to a saturating Holling type II response, whereas activation additionally modulated by local prey density produces a generalized sigmoidal Holling type III response. This is achieved by means of a diffusive scaling and a formal hydrodynamic limit, from which we derive a closed reaction-diffusion system of Rosenzweig-MacArthur type for the prey and total predator spatial densities.
item.dc:creator: Paolo Butt\`a

item.title: The effect of the permeability in interface problems: impermeable barriers and free diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2610.32607v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Focusing on reaction-diffusion models with an interface region dividing the domain, we study the stability of systems as the permeability parameter approaches zero or infinity under Kedem-Katchalsky boundary conditions imposed on the membrane or interface region. These boundary conditions establish that the flux across the interface manifold is proportional to the density jump across that region, with the constant of proportionality defined as the permeability parameter. We analyze both limiting behaviors: when permeability vanishes and when infinite flux is permitted. This analysis is carried out for both the well-known symmetric case, where permeability is identical in both directions across the membrane, and the asymmetric case, where it depends on the direction of the flux. For the asymmetric case, we obtain novel and surprising results that reveal a richer variety of behaviors in this class of interface problems and that differ from the scalar models.
item.dc:creator: Pablo \'Alvarez-Caudevilla, Cristina Br\"andle, M\'onica Molina-Becerra, Antonio Su\'arez

item.title: Inverse problems and continuity of heat content coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2610.32613v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the small-time asymptotic expansions for the Dirichlet and Open heat contents of convex planar domains. We prove that the small-time asymptotic expansion for the Open heat content can determine a triangle among triangles, a parallelogram among parallelograms, and an acute trapezium among acute trapezia of the same height. In addition, for a sequence of convex polygons converging to a convex set with smooth boundary in the sense of Hausdorff, we show that the coefficients of order $t$ in the small-time asymptotic expansions of the Dirichlet and the Open heat contents converge to those of the limiting set. While, for a sequence of convex sets with smooth boundary converging to a convex polygon in the sense of Hausdorff, we show that the coefficients of order $t$ do not converge to that of the limiting polygon.
item.dc:creator: Ryoki Endo, Katie Gittins, Jacob Walker

item.title: Sharpness transitions for weighted Triebel--Lizorkin Hardy inequalities with p < q
item.description: arXiv:2610.32671v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For fractional difference energies with two power weights and distinct inner and outer exponents, we determine regimes in which the constant generated by the homogeneous power is optimal and regimes in which it loses optimality. In the range $1<p<q$, we prove sharp Hardy inequalities on nontrivial weight intervals for every sign of $D=d+2\beta-sp$, including a two-sided interval in the balanced case $D=0$. For $q\ge2$, these intervals extend strictly beyond an elementary pointwise scalar criterion. For $1<p<q<2$, we determine the optimal power exponent in the scalar supporting-line inequality and obtain a larger explicit sharpness interval. The proof pairs opposite logarithmic displacements and controls the nonlinear deficit by a quadratic reference energy of the transformed function. Its translation estimate allows a positive contribution at bounded scales to absorb negative contributions at remote scales. Concentrating tests prove strict loss of homogeneous sharpness near both finite-energy endpoints, and angular variations give concrete bounds for the first sharpness threshold. We extend the method to flat singular sets and regional half-space energies, retaining the distinction between ambient finite-energy conditions and finiteness of the homogeneous candidate. We also treat the complementary order $p>q$, including flat-subspace inequalities and a complete alternative proof for point singularities. All sharpness sequences belong to the specified smooth test classes, and every positive optimal constant extends to their completion in the difference norm.
item.dc:creator: Yongyang Jin, Li Tang

item.title: Finitely many solutions for the prescribed scalar curvature problem at the critical flatness order
item.description: arXiv:2610.32707v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the following prescribed scalar curvature problem $$ -\Delta u=K(y)u^{2^*-1},\ \ u>0 \,\ \ \text{in}\ \ \mathbb{R}^N, \tag*{$(*)$} $$ where $2^*=\frac{2N}{N-2}$. For $N\geq4$, we construct a positive $K(y)$ with maximum set $\{|y|=1\}$ and critical order of flatness $m=N-2$ at $|y|=1$, such that problem $(*)$ admits only finitely many positive solutions in $D^{1,2}(\mathbb{R}^N)$. To this end, we prove compactness of the solution set of $(*)$ by blow-up analysis and then apply Sard's theorem to choose $K$ for which each solution is nondegenerate and hence isolated, so that the solution set of $(*)$ is finite. Our results give a negative answer to Wei--Yan's conjecture in [J. Wei and S. Yan, JFA, 2010].
item.dc:creator: Wei Ji, Yixing Pu

item.title: Corner Regularity and Asymptotics for the Two-Dimensional Radiation Transport Equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.32732v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The regularity of solutions to the two-dimensional radiation transport equation plays a central role in understanding the behavior of scalar flux near geometric corners. In a previous study of Kaper's corner singularity problem, the physical transport kernel was decomposed into its principal inverse-distance singularity and a lower-order remainder, reducing the corner asymptotic analysis to the question of whether the scalar flux possesses sufficient continuity to justify differentiation of the associated singular potential. The required regularity, however, remained unresolved. In this paper, we establish a sharp modulus-of-continuity estimate for the scalar flux generated by the physical transport kernel and prove the estimate $\omega_{\phi}(h)=O\!\left(h\log(D/h)\right)$, which implies Dini continuity. This estimate yields absolute convergence of the fluctuation term arising in the differentiated principal potential and permits a rigorous differentiation formula for transport solutions. Using this regularity framework, we derive the fixed-angle asymptotic behavior of the scalar flux and its first derivatives near a rectangular corner. For every fixed interior ray, the gradient exhibits logarithmic growth, while the scalar flux admits an $r\log(1/r)$ correction with an explicitly identified coefficient determined by the corner values of the flux and source. The analysis shows that a rectangular corner does not generate a singularity stronger than the logarithmic first-derivative singularity already present in smooth-boundary transport theory. Numerical calculations on benchmark problems are consistent with the theoretical predictions. These results provide a rigorous resolution of the regularity issue underlying Kaper's corner singularity problem and establish a mathematical framework for corner asymptotics in two-dimensional radiation transport.
item.dc:creator: Dean Wang

item.title: Homogenization of the Stokes equations in a domain perforated by a thin truss
item.description: arXiv:2610.32804v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the homogenization problem of the stationary Stokes equations in a periodically perforated domain whose solid structure consists of a thin truss. That is, the width $a_\epsilon$ of the truss tends to zero faster than the period size $\epsilon$. We identify the different scaling regimes and derive the corresponding effective equations. In the critical regime, we obtain the Brinkman equations, while in the subcritical regime, we recover the unchanged Stokes equations. In a subrange of the supercritical regime, we derive Darcy's law as the effective equation. Furthermore, we explicitly compute the effective coefficients in the Darcy and Brinkman limits. Moreover, as a tool in the analysis, we establish the analogous homogenization result for a periodic forest of cylinders. Finally, we also consider the homogenization result for a fence of cylinders.
item.dc:creator: Pascal Hadr\'e, Richard M. H\"ofer

item.title: The Two-Dimensional Narrow Escape Problem with Deterministic Initial Condition: Mean Escape Time and Escape location probabilities
item.description: arXiv:2610.32829v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a rigorous asymptotic analysis of the two-dimensional narrow escape problem for a Brownian particle initiated at a deterministic position x. While we address the mean escape time, the main novelty lies in our derivation of the asymptotic escape distribution. We derive explicit asymptotic formulas that characterize the dependence of the escape behavior on the relative configuration of the starting point and the window centers. These results remain valid as the starting position approaches the boundary windows and include refined error estimates. The formulas are obtained with two independent methods, each of them having their own interest. A central feature of this work is the rigorous treatment of the underlying mixed boundary value problems in the absence of a contact angle at the escape window boundaries. By leveraging recent results on the maximal regularity of the gradient of the solutions of such mixed boundary value problems, we ensure the analytical validity of our approach despite the inherent loss of regularity of these solutions at the escape window boundaries. Finally, we apply these general results to provide a full sharp asymptotic equivalents for regimes where window sizes scale at specific relative rates.
item.dc:creator: Lo\"is Delande (AGM - UMR 8088), Tony Leli\`evre (CERMICS), Boris Nectoux (LMBP), Thomas Normand

item.title: Self-similar solutions for the gSQG patch equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.32857v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The inviscid generalized surface quasi-geostrophic (gSQG) equations are a family of active scalar equations parametrized by a scalar $\alpha$ that includes the two-dimensional Euler equations ($\alpha = 0)$ and the SQG equation $(\alpha = 1)$. We prove that, for every $\alpha \in (\frac{7}{4}, 2)$ and every $T > 0$, there exists a self-similar patch solution whose boundary is a smooth, unbounded graph for $0 \leq t < T$ and develops a corner singularity at time $T$.
item.dc:creator: Javier Gomez-Serrano, Marcus Pasquariello

item.title: Hardy inequalities on the positive integer lattice: a dimensional transition
item.description: arXiv:2610.32858v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine exactly in which dimensions the sharp Hardy coefficient on the positive integer lattice agrees with that on the positive Euclidean cone, with Dirichlet conditions on every coordinate face. Equality holds in dimensions one and two, whereas the discrete coefficient is strictly smaller in every dimension at least three. An exact transformation identifies the lattice problem with a weighted Dirichlet problem on a cube. A tangential integration identity evaluates the defect of an explicit critical profile and proves the dimensional transition. The continuous coefficient remains the lower edge of the essential spectrum of the transformed operator; below that edge, the sharp discrete coefficient is a simple eigenvalue with a positive eigenfunction. In dimension three, an explicit supersolution places the coefficient strictly between twelve and forty-nine quarters. A representation on a product of three-dimensional spheres relates the spectral threshold to the local geometry of the transformed problem.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Lizama

item.title: From entropy waves to vortex sheets for the Euler equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.32893v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct piecewise smooth solutions of the full compressible Euler equations that evolve from entropy waves into vortex sheets while retaining a strictly positive Taylor jump. For every integer $\kappa\geq1$, we obtain solutions satisfying initial material compatibility for pressure and velocity through order $\kappa$, whose tangential velocity jump has a nonzero leading term of order $t^{\kappa+1}$. These solutions are periodic in the tangential variables and admit a smooth realization in a slab with impermeable walls. We also construct solutions on a local nonperiodic tangential patch that satisfy initial material compatibility at every order, yet have a tangential velocity jump that is nonzero for every sufficiently small positive time and flat at $t=0$. The finite-order construction uses a normal Cauchy-Kowalevski problem for velocity potentials, whereas the all-order construction uses a homogeneous reduction to a smooth hyperbolic Cauchy problem.
item.dc:creator: Yuri Trakhinin, Wei Wang, Zhifei Zhang, Wenbin Zhao

item.title: Stationary bistable fronts on a periodic necklace graph: existence, stability and multiplicity
item.description: arXiv:2610.32917v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study stationary fronts for a bistable reaction-diffusion equation with the McKean reaction on a periodic necklace metric graph. For profiles that agree on each pair of parallel edges, the problem reduces to a scalar equation on the real line with a periodic, piecewise constant diffusion coefficient. The diffusion contrast of the necklace is not small, so the coefficient cannot be treated as a small perturbation of a constant. Because the McKean reaction is piecewise linear, the equation is affine between threshold crossings and coefficient interfaces, and a front is determined explicitly by its crossing points. We find an explicit interval of reaction thresholds, the pinning interval, such that stationary fronts, monotone or not, exist exactly for thresholds in this interval. Up to translations by the spatial period, there are exactly two decreasing fronts at each interior threshold and one front at each endpoint. For each fixed interior threshold, one decreasing front is Lyapunov stable and the other is unstable in the $W^{1,\infty}(\mathbb{R})$ norm, among mild solutions with one continuously moving threshold crossing. The crossing phases of the two decreasing fronts also determine nonmonotone fronts. For each interior threshold and odd $m\geq3$, choose $m$ periods of the coefficient that are sufficiently far apart. There are then exactly $2^m$ fronts with one threshold crossing in each chosen period and none elsewhere. Varying the chosen periods gives infinitely many inequivalent fronts with $m$ crossings.
item.dc:creator: Yoichiro Mori, Toshiyuki Ogawa, Chanoknun Sintavanuruk

item.title: Hot Spots: From Smooth to Nonsmooth Simply Connected Planar Domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.32920v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Assuming the absence of interior local extrema for first positive Neumann eigenfunctions on bounded smooth simply connected planar domains, as reported in \cite{SmoothInput}, we extend the hot spots conclusion to simply connected domains of finite area with compact Sobolev embedding and simple first positive Neumann eigenvalue. The supremum and infimum are approached in arbitrarily thin boundary layers. For bounded domains and eigenfunctions continuous up to the boundary, both extrema are attained on the boundary. We also transfer polynomial Neumann heat-kernel bounds uniformly along a conformal exhaustion and construct explicit bounded and unbounded examples, including domains with cusps and a domain with infinitely many corners and bottlenecks. Some of these examples admit no polynomial Neumann heat-kernel bound.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Ban\~nuelos

item.title: Modified scattering for the 3D Hartree equation with singular external potentials
item.description: arXiv:2610.32939v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish modified scattering for the three-dimensional Hartree equation with Coulomb interaction and singular external potentials, including repulsive Coulomb and inverse-square potentials. In the defocusing case, the result holds for arbitrary initial data in $H^{0,1}(\mathbb R^3)\cap H^{1,0}(\mathbb R^3)$. In particular, we obtain large-data modified scattering for the flat defocusing Hartree equation. For the focusing problem with repulsive Coulomb potential $V(x)=\kappa|x|^{-1}$, we prove radial modified scattering under the sharp mass condition $|\lambda|\|u_0\|_2^2\leq 2\kappa$, including the endpoint, and construct standing waves at every larger mass. Our argument obtains strong $L^2$ convergence from rescaled energy and comparison with a frozen-field evolution.
item.dc:creator: Mengyi Xie

item.title: Collapsed translating solitons with planar wings
item.description: arXiv:2610.31669v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study complete embedded translating solitons in R^3 with finite genus and finite entropy. We prove that such collapsed translators whose wings are all of planar type (in a weak topological sense) must be vertical flat planes. In particular, this implies the non-existence result for gluing and doubling constructions involving planes that was conjectured in (14) and announced in (9) as an application of the authors' techniques, under weaker assumptions than previous rigidity results by Khan and Lynch-Tinaglia in (17,19,20). A key ingredient is a sharp new a priori decay estimate in the exterior problem for the horizontal graphical translator equation, showing that bounded solutions to the nonlinear equation, and their gradients, are controlled by multiples of the Green's function of the linear drift Laplacian, regardless of the size of the given L^\infty data. Combined with a graphical description of the infinite ends and the Neves-Tian flux identity, this yields the main rigidity result. As another application, we obtain a full classification of collapsed embedded finite-genus translators of entropy lambda < 3.
item.dc:creator: Eddygledson Souza Gama, Francisco Mart\'in, Niels Martin M{\o}ller

item.title: Rapid stabilization for Stokes and Navier-Stokes systems with localized disturbance
item.description: arXiv:2610.31790v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this study, we analyze the rapid stabilization of Stokes and the two- and three-dimensional Navier-Stokes systems in the presence of an unknown spatially localized disturbance. A multivalued feedback control strategy is proposed which combines the Lyapunov frequency method with the multivalued sign operator. This methodology connects Lyapunov-based stability analysis with spectral inequalities, while the inclusion of the sign operator provides robustness against disturbance. The closed-loop system is governed by a differential inclusion, for which well-posedness is proved via the theory of maximal monotone operators. This approach guarantees global rapid exponential stabilization for the Stokes system and local rapid exponential stabilization for the two- and three-dimensional Navier-Stokes systems, with arbitrarily large disturbance bounds. In three dimensions, we obtain global strong solutions and rapid exponential stabilization for initial data sufficiently small in the $L^2$-norm with a prescribed, arbitrarily large bound in the $H^1$-norm.
item.dc:creator: Christian Calle, Patricio Guzm\'an, Hugo Parada, Jefferson Prada

item.title: Observability from measurable sets for strongly coupled parabolic systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.31876v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We characterize observability of strongly coupled parabolic systems from arbitrary space-time measurable sets of positive measure. For constant coercive diffusion matrices and arbitrary constant zeroth-order coupling and observation matrices, observability holds if and only if the generalized Kalman rank condition is satisfied at every Dirichlet eigenvalue. The diffusion matrix need not be diagonalizable, and the number of components is arbitrary. The observation is measured in $L^1$, yielding null controllability with bounded controls by duality. The proof combines a Remez-type inequality for exponential polynomials with a quantitative analysis of the mode-dependent Kalman condition. The resulting finite-dimensional observability estimate is uniform over the spatial modes up to a polynomial frequency loss. A spectral inequality and the Lebeau--Robbiano strategy then give observability of the full system.
item.dc:creator: Xinyi Chen, K\'evin Le Balc'h

item.title: Optimal Graphon Control of Collective Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.31975v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study optimal control of non-linear graphon dynamics in which the interaction kernel itself is the control. Motivated by opinion formation in social networks, we ask how changing who influences whom can steer a population toward a desired outcome. We develop a framework using interaction kernels with bounded variation in the receiver label, providing compactness while accommodating finite networks. We prove existence of an optimal pair and show that finite-agent approximations recover the continuum optimal value under successive refinement of the network and initial data, with subsequential convergence of suitably chosen discrete optimizers. Numerical experiments use neural networks to approximate optimal controls for bounded-confidence and graphon Kuramoto dynamics, illustrating how changes in interactions can prevent fragmentation and promote synchronization.
item.dc:creator: Joseph K. Miller, Brandon Su

item.title: A Dynamic Inventory Rationing Model for Last-Mile Delivery of Medication in Liberia's Community Health Program
item.description: arXiv:2610.32051v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the dynamic allocation of scarce medications in Liberia's community health program. A central warehouse supplies a health facility and the Community Health Assistants (CHAs) it supervises. When a CHA runs out of medication, patients are referred to the facility, incurring travel costs if they complete the referral and remain untreated otherwise. Allocating inventory to CHAs allows more patients to receive treatment without traveling, while retaining inventory centrally preserves flexibility to respond to uncertain demand. The allocation problem must balance these considerations while accounting for fairness across locations. We formulate this problem as a finite-horizon stochastic control problem whose objective combines the costs of referrals and untreated patients with a demand-weighted fairness utility. Because standard dynamic programming methods are computationally intractable in this setting, we develop a continuous-time approximation that involves controlling the drift rate of a reflected Brownian motion. We then adapt the deep splitting method, using deep neural networks to approximate the value function and its gradient and compute a dynamic allocation policy. We calibrate the model using data on malaria cases among children in the Fangonda region of Lofa County, Liberia, and evaluate the proposed policy in the original discrete-time model. In the baseline setting, our policy reduces operating costs by about 6% relative to the strongest benchmark, the fairness-only policy, while retaining approximately 98% of its fairness utility. Additional experiments show that higher referral costs shift inventory toward CHAs and reduce local unmet demand, while greater demand variability increases our policy's performance over the fairness-only benchmark. Our model and computational approach provide a framework for studying similar last-mile allocation problems.
item.dc:creator: Baris Ata, Yufan Chen, Robert Montgomery

item.title: The elastic figure-eight knot is not planar
item.description: arXiv:2610.32320v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that every elastic knot in any non-torus twist knot class is not planar. In particular, this disproves a numerically motivated planarity conjecture for elastic figure-eight knots.
item.dc:creator: Tatsuya Miura

item.title: Riesz Transform Bounds Imply Parabolic Uniform Rectifiability of Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.32534v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that if a $(k+2)$-Ahlfors--David regular measure $\mu$ in parabolic space $\mathbb P^n$ has support equal to a parabolic Lipschitz graph with sufficiently small Lipschitz constant, and the parabolic Riesz transform is bounded on $L^2(\mu)$, then $\mu$ is parabolic uniformly rectifiable and the graph is regular parabolic Lipschitz. The result holds for every integer $0\leq k\leq n-1$.
item.dc:creator: John Hoffman

item.title: A direct proof of the equivalence of the A2 and the Helson--Szego conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.32922v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a direct proof of the equivalence between the Muckenhoupt $\mathcal{A}_2$ and the Helson--Szeg\H{o} conditions on the unit circle $T$. A positive weight $w$ belongs to $\mathcal{A}_2(T)$ if and only if $\log w=u+Hv$, where $u,v$ are real bounded functions, $\|v\|_\infty<\frac{\pi}{2}$, and $H$ denotes the periodic Hilbert transform. The classical proof combines the Helson--Szeg\H{o} theorem with the Hunt--Muckenhoupt--Wheeden characterization of weighted boundedness of the Hilbert transform. Our proof derives the Helson--Szeg\H{o} representation directly from the Muckenhoupt $\mathcal{A}_2$ condition, without using boundedness of $H$ on $L^2(w)$.
item.dc:creator: Christos Grigoriadis, Michail Paparizos, Georgios Psaromiligkos

item.title: Nonexistence results for the semilinear wave equation on graphs
item.description: arXiv:2506.08697v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the semilinear wave equation with potential on weighted graphs. We establish sufficient conditions for the nonexistence of global-in-time solutions. Both nonnegative and sign-changing solutions are considered. In particular, the proof for sign-changing solutions relies on a novel technique for this type of result.
item.dc:creator: Dario Daniele Monticelli, Fabio Punzo, Jacopo Somaglia

item.title: The Hardy spaces $\mathcal{H}^{p}_{FIO}(\mathbb{R}^{n})$ for Fourier integral operators for $p<1$
item.description: arXiv:2508.13243v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce the Hardy spaces $\mathcal{H}^{p}_{FIO}(\mathbb{R}^{n})$ for Fourier integral operators for $0<p<1$, thereby extending earlier constructions for $1\leq p\leq \infty$. We then establish various properties of these spaces, including their behavior under complex interpolation and duality, and their invariance under Fourier integral operators. We also obtain Sobolev embeddings, equivalent characterizations, and a molecular decomposition. These spaces are used in the companion article arXiv:2502.02511 to determine the sharp $\mathcal{H}^{1}(\mathbb{R}^{n})$ and $\mathrm{bmo}(\mathbb{R}^{n})$ regularity of wave equations with rough coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Naijia Liu, Jan Rozendaal, Liang Song

item.title: Application of Onsager's Variational Principle to the Navier-Stokes Equations
item.description: arXiv:2509.24033v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this note we propose a basic $L^2$-based approach for studying the global and local energy equalities of the incompressible 3D Navier-Stokes equations in the standard energy class on $\mathbb{T}^3 \times (0,T]$. Motivated by L. Onsager's principle of least dissipation of energy (1931), we give a new sufficient condition for the energy equalities in terms of the limit of a sequence of minimizers. In particular, we show that the equalities are attained if this limit is non-vanishing. We observe that the indeterminacy in the vanishing case is reminiscent of turbulence-driven energy transfer dominating other transport processes.
item.dc:creator: Hamid A. Said

item.title: Hyperbolic Monge-Amp\`ere Equation on a Cylinder: Well-Posedness and Stability
item.description: arXiv:2509.25553v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper develops a rigorous analytic framework for the hyperbolic Monge-Amp\`ere equation on strip-like domains, which model wrinkled patterns in thin elastic sheets. Our work addresses the rigid side of the classical rigidity-flexibility dichotomy by defining this regime not by high smoothness, but by the more fundamental property of partial convexity. The hodograph transformation is the natural tool for this setting, as its validity is predicated on partial convexity. It converts the nonlinear Monge-Amp\`ere equation into a linear damped wave equation, allowing us to formulate a well-posed Cauchy-Goursat problem. A key challenge is the corner singularity that arises where characteristic and non-characteristic boundary data meet. To resolve this, we develop a parametrix-corrector decomposition that captures the solution's inherent singular behavior. This method recasts the problem as a singular Volterra integral equation, for which we prove the existence and uniqueness of a new class of hodograph weak solutions. Finally, we derive energy estimates to establish the quantitative stability of these rigid solutions under perturbations of the underlying curvature function.
item.dc:creator: Maria Deliyianni, Shankar C. Venkataramani

item.title: Homogenization of a thin linear elastic plate reinforced with a periodic mosaic of small rigid plates
item.description: arXiv:2512.01042v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the framework of linearized elasticity, we study thin elastic composite plates with thickness $\delta$. The plates contain small, rigid rectangular plates distributed periodically along $\varepsilon$. Between two neighboring rigid plates is an elastic beam with thickness $\delta < \varepsilon/3 < 1$. Through a simultaneous process of homogenization and dimension reduction, we obtain the limit model. Our analysis yields Korn-type inequalities adapted to the rigid-elastic geometry of the structure and provides a precise characterization of the limit deformation and displacement fields. In the $2$D limit problem, the bending is the sum of two functions, each depending on only one variable. This is due to the fact that the mixed derivatives of the outer-plane displacement vanish. Finally, the limiting 2D problem is two decoupled plates or strips, each one with just three degrees of freedom: shear along the strip axis, the cross-contraction (-extension), and the cross-bending. The corresponding correctors are defined in the same way in the periodicity cell. In the linearized setting, all the correctors are decomposed.
item.dc:creator: Amartya Chakrabortty, Georges Griso, Julia Orlik

item.title: A Li-Yau and Aronson-B\'enilan approach for the Keller-Segel system with critical exponent
item.description: arXiv:2512.17772v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Li-Yau and Aronson-B\'enilan estimates are fundamental differential inequalities for heat and porous-medium equations, yielding differential Harnack inequalities and sharp smoothing and decay rates. We develop analogues for the critical parabolic-elliptic Keller-Segel system on $\mathbb{R}^d$, where diffusion and aggregation act at the same scale. Our main tool is the effective pressure $v=p-u$, with $p=\log\rho$ in $d=2$ and $p=\frac{m}{m-1}\rho^{m-1}$ for $d>2$, $m=2-\frac{2}{d}$. We prove quantitative lower bounds on $\Delta v$, showing that classical pressure estimates subsist in a suitable form despite the nonlocal interaction. These estimates unify previous results and yield new regularity. For nonnegative finite-measure initial data of sufficiently small mass, assuming only a logarithmic moment in $d=2$, we construct global solutions smooth for positive times and satisfying $\|\rho_t\|_{L^\infty}\le C/t$. For finite-free-energy data, we obtain global $L^\infty$ bounds of order $1+t^{-1}$ in the subcritical and critical mass regimes. We also introduce a new characterization of the critical mass as the minimal mass $M_c^{\mathrm{sub}}(d)$ of subsolutions of the elliptic Lane-Emden equation (Liouville in $d=2$). We prove that it equals $8\pi$ in dimension $2$ and, for $d\ge3$, coincides with the Keller-Segel critical mass given by the HLS inequality, by reducing the problem to a one-dimensional optimal-control problem. Along the way we prove tools of independent interest: $L^\infty$ estimates from lower bounds on $\Delta v$, critical log-HLS/HLS estimates away from Dirac masses, Hessian bounds for Newtonian potentials, and Lipschitz and Hessian estimates for bounded porous-medium solutions with drifts on the whole space.
item.dc:creator: Charles Elbar, Alejandro Fern\'andez-Jim\'enez, Filippo Santambrogio

item.title: Self-similar finite-time blowups with singular profiles of the generalized Constantin-Lax-Majda model: theoretical and numerical investigations
item.description: arXiv:2603.25104v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For the generalized Constantin-Lax-Majda model with a parameter $a$, we investigate novel scenarios of self-similar finite-time blowups that arise from a new setting where the smooth initial data satisfy a certain derivative degeneracy condition. In this setting, our numerical study reveals distinct self-similar blowup behaviors depending on the sign of $a$. For $a>0$, we observe one-scale self-similar blowups with regular profiles that have not been found in previous studies. In contrast, for $a\le 0$, we discover a novel two-scale self-similar blowup scenario where the outer profile converges to a singular function at the blowup time while the inner profile remains regular on a much smaller scale. Correspondingly, an $a$-parameterized family of singular self-similar profiles with explicit expressions are constructed for $a<0$ and shown to match nicely with the limiting profiles obtained in numerical simulation. In particular, for the specific case of $a=0$, we rigorously prove the convergence of the outer profile to an explicit singular function in self-similar coordinates. Furthermore, we demonstrate the two-scale nature of the blowup in this scenario by showing that the local inner profile behavior around the singularity point of the outer profile is governed by a traveling wave on a smaller scale. To support this observation, we rigorously establish the existence of such traveling wave solutions via a fixed-point method.
item.dc:creator: De Huang, Jiajun Tong, Xiuyuan Wang

item.title: Minimizers for the Cahn-Hilliard energy functional with the Flory-Huggins potential under strong anchoring conditions
item.description: arXiv:2604.19590v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we theoretically and numerically study the minimizers for the Cahn-Hilliard energy with the Flory-Huggins potential under the strong anchoring condition, i.e., the Dirichlet boundary condition. We reveal bifurcation phenomena mediated by the boundary condition, the transition layer thickness, and the temperature of the system. Numerical simulations are also presented to approximate the minimizers of this energy by solving a gradient-flow equation, namely the Allen-Cahn equation constrained with strong anchoring conditions and random initial data. The effects of varying the transition layer thickness and temperature are presented to confirm the theoretical analysis.
item.dc:creator: Shibin Dai, Abba Ramadan, Natasha Sharma

item.title: Correctness of Biot's model of in situ leaching for incompressible liquid and compressible solid components
item.description: arXiv:2604.22645v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a mathematical model of in situ leaching of rare metals, in which the joint filtration of two liquids is governed by the microscopic model $\mathbb{A}^{\varepsilon}$. A key difficulty is the unknown (free) boundary $\Gamma(r)$ between solid and liquid components, determined by an additional condition on $\Gamma(r)$; no standard methods exist for this nonlinear problem. To resolve it, we apply the fixed point theorem. For a given function $r(\boldsymbol{x},t)$ from a set $\mathfrak{M}_{(0,T)}$ of sufficiently smooth functions describing the skeleton structure, we consider the auxiliary problem $\mathbb{B}^{\varepsilon}(r)$: an elliptic system for displacements of the liquid and solid components coupled with parabolic equations for the acid concentration. Selecting the weak solution of minimal smoothness, we apply the homogenization method to pass from the microscopic to the macroscopic description. The resulting macroscopic model $\mathbb{H}(r)$ contains a homogenized boundary condition that expresses the normal boundary velocity $V_{N}=\partial r/\partial t$ as a linear function of the acid concentration $c$. Since $c$ depends on $r$ via an operator $\mathbb{F}\colon\mathfrak{M}_{(0,T)}\to\mathfrak{M}_{(0,T)}$, we prove that $\mathbb{F}$ is Lipschitz continuous and, by Banach's theorem, possesses a unique fixed point $r^{*}$, which yields the unique solution $\mathbb{H}=\mathbb{H}(r^{*})$.
item.dc:creator: Anvarbek Meirmanov, Akbota Senkebayeva

item.title: Symmetry Breaking and Moduli for Ancient Yamabe Flows on the Sphere
item.description: arXiv:2606.22355v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For every $n\ge3$, we construct compact Type II ancient Yamabe flows in the round conformal class of the unit $n$-sphere $\Ss^n$. After stereographic projection and rescaling of time and conformal factor, the solutions are asymptotic backward in time to finite superpositions of Aubin--Talenti bubbles with mutually comparable scales. For integers $h\ge1$ and $k\ge2$, the limiting centers form $h$ coaxial regular $k$-gons; when $h\ge2$, their distinct layer heights may be prescribed arbitrarily in the interval $(-1,1)$. If $hk\ge3$, the resulting flows are not geometrically equivalent to any rotationally symmetric ancient flow. For each flow, there is a fixed point of $\Ss^n$ at which the Ricci tensor has both positive and negative eigenvalues on every time slice. The corresponding volume-normalized Yamabe flows are also ancient. After rescaling each time slice to a fixed volume, the metrics converge to a wedge of $hk$ isometric round $n$-spheres in the Gromov--Hausdorff topology, as time tends to $-\infty$. For fixed $h,k\ge2$, the concentration configurations admit an explicit $(h-1)$-parameter description up to M\"obius transformations. Consequently, the construction yields geometrically inequivalent flows indexed by a nonempty open subset of $\R^{h-1}$, all with the same fixed-volume backward Gromov--Hausdorff limit. The proof uses inner--outer gluing for the quasilinear parabolic equation in $n$-dimensional space that exhibits Kelvin symmetry. Weighted Euclidean and spherical H\"older estimates control the nonlinear terms and, together with parabolic regularity, yield smooth extension of the conformal metrics across the north pole of $\Ss^n$.
item.dc:creator: Haixia Chen, Seunghyeok Kim, Monica Musso

item.title: Boundary regularity of harmonic functions in $C^1$ slit domains
item.description: arXiv:2609.15923v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish precise upper and lower estimates for harmonic functions vanishing on the slit of a $C^1$ slit domain, with no assumption that the slit lies in a hyperplane. The classical $\sqrt{d}$ growth near the edge, $d$ being the distance to the slit, persists in this generality, up to an explicit factor \[\exp\Big( \pm C \int_\rho^r \omega(s)\, \frac{ds}{s} \Big)\] determined by the $C^1$-modulus of continuity $\omega$ of the slit, where $\rho < r$ are the two scales being compared. The upper estimates allow a right-hand side and non-zero boundary data. The correction factors remain bounded above and below by positive constants as $\rho\to0$ precisely when $\omega$ satisfies the Dini condition. Moduli of continuity beyond the Dini regime, as is the case for the logarithmic moduli arising at singular sets in relevant free boundary problems, were not covered by the previous $C^{1,\alpha}$ theory. Previously, the $\sqrt{d}$ growth was known for slits contained in a hyperplane, which additionally have a $C^{1,\alpha}$ edge (De Silva, Savin). For Lipschitz slits, there are boundary Harnack principles, but no growth rate is identified precisely. The main technical ingredient is a change of coordinates flattening a Lipschitz slit domain onto the model half-hyperplane slit, with quantitative estimates up to second order. The construction is geometric and does not use the equation, so we expect it to be useful for other boundary regularity problems.
item.dc:creator: Joan Domingo-Pasarin, Pablo Hidalgo-Palencia, Alejandro Mart\'inez, Clara Torres-Latorre

item.title: Bounds of singular sets for elliptic equations in $C^{1, Dini}$ domains with singular potentials
item.description: arXiv:2609.21988v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the quantitative codimension-two estimate for the singular set in the boundary neighborhoods of the solutions of \begin{equation*} \Delta u+V(x)u=0\qquad\text{in }\Omega, \qquad u=0\qquad\text{on }\partial\Omega, \end{equation*} where $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ is a bounded $C^{1,\mathrm{Dini}}$ domain and $V\in L^p(\Omega)$ for some $p>n$. We first prove the explicit upper bound for the doubling index is given by $C(n,p,\Omega)(1+\|V\|_{L^p(\Omega)}^{\frac{2p}{3p-2n}})$.The analytic input is an interior volume estimate for solutions of second order elliptic equations with uniformly elliptic Dini leading coefficients and $V\in L^p$. Using the quantitative doubling index bound, boundary flattening, we show an explicit upper bound for singular sets in the neighborhood of the boundary of the $C^{1,\mathrm{Dini}}$ domain.
item.dc:creator: Zhiwei Wang, Jiuyi Zhu

item.title: Asymptotic behavior of the one-dimensional Vlasov--Poisson system with a repulsive harmonic potential
item.description: arXiv:2610.02551v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the one-dimensional Vlasov--Poisson system with a repulsive harmonic potential. For repulsive self-interactions, we prove modified scattering for initial data of arbitrary size, assuming only velocity weights and one derivative; no smallness, symmetry, compact support, or spatial moments are required. In the lens variables of \cite{HK26}, the self-consistent force carries a nonintegrable time weight. We remove it by a momentum correction that solves a forced Burgers equation; the repulsive sign makes this correction monotone, which gives bounds for large data. We also construct modified wave operators for both signs of the interaction. Together with \cite{VR24,BVR25,HK26}, this gives a scattering theory in every dimension.
item.dc:creator: Wenrui Huang

item.title: Finite-time blow-up for the real-valued defocusing energy-supercritical NLW
item.description: arXiv:2610.06678v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the defocusing nonlinear wave equations $\partial_t^2u-\Delta u+u^p=0$, with $p$ odd, for real-valued functions on $\mathbb R^{1+d}$, in the energy-supercritical case. For $(d,p)=(9,3)$, $(7,5)$ and $(6,7)$, we construct a discretely self-similar solution in a backward light cone, of the form $$u(t,x)=(T-t)^{-\frac{2}{p-1}}W^*\big(\omega^*\log\frac1{T-t},\frac{|x|}{T-t}\big),$$ where the nonzero profile $W^*$ is $2\pi$-periodic in its first variable and real-analytic up to and across the light cone. Cutting off its initial data gives smooth, compactly supported, radial data whose solution coincides with the discretely self-similar solution in the backward light cone, is smooth on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^{d}$ except at the vertex $(T,0)$ of the cone, and blows up there at the self-similar rate. The solutions we construct here appear to be the first blow-up solutions of defocusing energy-supercritical NLW with smooth real-valued data. For comparison, we also give in an appendix, for every energy-supercritical exponent, a construction of a bounded, finite-energy, radial solution which is continuously self-similar in a backward light cone and whose supremum blows up; it is not smooth across the light cone, and the difficulty of the problem lies entirely in this regularity. Existence of the real profile is proved by a computer-assisted Newton--Kantorovich argument in a Banach algebra of Fourier--Chebyshev coefficients, with rigorous error control. The main analytic ingredients are an exact description of the mode operators for the linear part, which are hypergeometric and upper triangular in the Chebyshev basis, and a bound for their inverses that is uniform at high frequencies. All computer-assisted proofs, including the requisite codes and the approximate objects, are accessible on GitHub at \cite{code}.
item.dc:creator: Matthieu Cadiot, Alexandru D. Ionescu, Stan Palasek

item.title: Shape optimisation of the maximum of the gradient of the torsion function on convex sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.08408v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We analyse the boundary behaviour of the gradient of the torsion function $w_\Om$ in convex domains $\Om\subset\mathbb{R}^d$. We prove that its $L^\infty$-norm is attained at a boundary point and establish the stability of this norm under general (convex) perturbations. For problems of the form $$\sup\{\|\nabla w_{\Om}\|_\infty: \Om \subset \R^d,\textup{open, bounded and convex}, G(\Om)=m\},$$ where $G$ is either volume or perimeter, we show the existence of maximisers which are $C^1$-smooth, rotationally symmetric about an axis and contain a $(d-1)$- dimensional ball (of estimated size) in their boundary. Other constraints, whether geometric (such as diameter or circumradius) or variational (such as torsion or first Dirichlet eigenvalue), are also briefly discussed, and some of their characteristic behaviours are highlighted.
item.dc:creator: Michiel van den Berg, Dorin Bucur, Mickael Nahon

item.title: Uniqueness for tv-regularized inverse problems with source in divergence form
item.description: arXiv:2610.11719v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Inverse source problems in divergence form consist in finding a vector field with prescribed support S, whose divergence is the Laplacian of some observed potential. In this paper, we assume the unknown vector field is a vector-valued measure, and we study the corresponding least square inversion problems, regularized by penalizing the total variation, without discretizing the criterion nor the unknown. We prove that this problem has a unique minimizer in the case where S is a slender set; i.e., it has zero Lebesgue measure and each connected component of its complement has infinite Lebesgue measure. The proof relies on a refinement of Smirnov's decomposition of divergence-free measures [62] which is of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: L Baratchart (FACTAS), D P Hardin, C Villalobos-Guill\'en

item.title: Global solutions to the compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations in the half-space
item.description: arXiv:2610.15588v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the initial boundary value problem for the compressible Navier--Stokes--Poisson equations without damping in the three-dimensional half-space and in smooth exterior domains. The velocity satisfies the no-slip boundary condition, and the electric potential satisfies the homogeneous Neumann boundary condition. For small perturbations of a constant state in $H^3$, with a small initial electric field in $L^2$, we establish global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions. The uniform estimates combine density dissipation, tangential and normal derivative estimates, and a modified energy expressed through the Helmholtz projection. In exterior domains, boundary normal coordinates and localized elliptic estimates control the geometric terms. We also obtain algebraic decay in the full energy norm. In the half-space, finite tangential negative Sobolev norms of order $-s$, with $\frac12\leq s<1$, yield the rate $(1+t)^{-s/2}$. In exterior domains, integrable initial density and velocity perturbations yield the same form of estimate for $0<s<\frac14$. The exterior decay proof uses whole-space negative-order estimates for localized variables and the time integrability of the dissipation.

arXiv:2610.20976v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This third paper in a series on a parabolic-elliptic chemotaxis model studies bifurcation of positive constant equilibria in one space dimension. We consider $$ \left\{  egin{array}{ll} u_t=\Delta u-\chi_0

u u^\gamma, & x\in\Omega,\  rac{\partial u}{\partial n}= rac{\partial v}{\partial n}=0, & x\in\partial\Omega, \end{array} ight. $$ where $\Omega$ is a bounded interval, $\alpha,\gamma,m,\mu,
u>0$, $\chi_0\in\mathbb R$, and $a,b, eta\ge0$. Building on earlier results on global existence, boundedness, persistence, and stabilization, we take $\chi_0$ as the bifurcation parameter and examine the effects of $ eta$ and the domain size on the bifurcation. Center manifold reduction yields a coefficient $ eta_{n_0}$ at a simple bifurcation mode $n_0$ of a positive constant equilibrium. The pitchfork bifurcation is supercritical if $ eta_{n_0}>0$ and subcritical if $ eta_{n_0}<0$. Stronger desensitization raises the sensitivity required for loss of linear stability. Bifurcation may be supercritical for small $ eta$ but is always subcritical for sufficiently large $ eta$. Thus, desensitization makes patterns harder to trigger and favors abrupt rather than continuous emergence. The bifurcation mode increases with domain size, allowing more complex spatial patterns. Under suitable conditions, we prove unbounded continuation of local bifurcation branches. We also show that large-sensitivity stationary sequences satisfying a peak-gap hypothesis develop spike-like profiles. Numerical continuation and time-evolution experiments illustrate the bifurcating branches and spike-like solutions and suggest unbounded continuation and increasingly sharp stationary profiles.

item.title: Wave breaking for the nonlocal Whitham-type equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.27832v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we investigate wave breaking for the nonlocal Whitham-type equations. We establish more general wave breaking criteria that strictly extend earlier wave breaking criteria for the nonlocal Whitham-type equations. The approach relies on analyzing the monotonicity and continuity properties of a linear combination comprising the supremum and infimum of the solution's slope. Further generalizations are demonstrated via applications to the Camassa-Holm equation, the $\mu$-Camassa-Holm equation and the hyperelastic rod equation. Our refined approach yields more precise wave breaking criteria, thereby extending the theoretical understanding of singularity formation in dispersive waves.
item.dc:creator: Jian Chen, Shaojie Yang, Zhaoyang Yin

item.title: On the Allen--Cahn equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.28080v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Using the framework developed by OpenAI, we prove that finite Morse index implies $O(R^{n-1})$ energy growth for bounded entire solutions of the quartic Allen--Cahn equation in dimensions $4\leq n\leq9$, uniformly in the center of the ball. Combined with the cited finite-index classification results, this gives planar rigidity for $4\leq n\leq7$ and, for nonconstant solutions, multiplicity-one stable minimal cone blowdowns through dimension nine. Within the framework, we derive an additive adjacent-layer interaction estimate, a weighted curvature and defect estimate with exponent $p=9/4$, and the localization needed for exterior stability. The limiting interaction coefficient $48$ is sharp in the unrestricted low-defect class with sufficiently large logarithmic selection depth.
item.dc:creator: Zhouyu Long, Wenming Zou

item.title: Homogenization of the Stokes equations with slender bodies
item.description: arXiv:2610.31480v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we study the convergence of solutions of the Stokes equations in a domain perforated by slender bodies placed on a fixed periodic grid of size $2\epsilon$ as the size of the bodies goes to zero and the number of bodies goes to infinity. We assume that the width $b_\epsilon$ of the bodies vanishes faster than the length $a_\epsilon$ of the particles. We identify the critical scaling regimes for $a_\epsilon$ and $b_\epsilon$ and prove that in this case the system is effectively described by the Brinkman equations.
item.dc:creator: Pascal Hadr\'e, Richard M. H\"ofer

item.title: A H\"ormander spectral multiplier theorem for fractional Hardy operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.31532v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the fractional Laplacian with added critical or subcritical Hardy potential, called Hardy operator. We prove a H\"ormander spectral multiplier theorem, i.e., the boundedness of sufficiently smooth multipliers of these Hardy operators on Lebesgue spaces. The range of admissible Lebesgue exponents is optimal, but the smoothness assumption is probably not. The proof combines the Helffer--Sj\"ostrand formula with a quantitative Jaffard lemma for operator-valued matrices.
item.dc:creator: Konstantin Merz

item.title: Envelopes of Horospheres and Weingarten Surfaces in Hyperbolic 3-Space
item.description: arXiv:2401.12115v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We derive basic differential geometric formulae for surfaces in hyperbolic space represented as envelopes of horospheres. The dual notion of parallel hypersurfaces is also studied. The representation is applied to prove existence and regularity theorems for Weingarten surfaces in H^3, which satisfy (1-a)K = a(2-H), for an a < 0, and have a specified boundary curve at infinity. These surfaces are shown to be closely connected to conformal mappings of domains in S^2 into the unit disk and provide Riemannian interpretations for some conformal invariants associated to such mappings. This paper was originally written in 1984, before I learned to use TeX, and was typed by one of the secretaries in the Princeton Math Department. It was more or less, my first original work after my dissertation. For some reason, I was not able to get this paper published in a timely manner. The results and perspective in this paper have proved to be useful to a variety of people, some of whom asked me to render the article into TeX and post it to the arXiv. I had been seriously thinking about doing this, when Martin Bridgeman sent me a transcription of my original article into TeX. I am extremely grateful to him for the effort he has put into this project. The paper is now formatted in a more or less modern AMS-article style, but for lots of additional punctuation, a few corrections and some minor stylistic changes, the content has been largely reproduced as it originally was. Remarks about the 'state-of-the-art' in hyperbolic geometry are obviously way out of date, as there has been enormous progress in many aspects of this still rich subject.
